To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we show that label shift adaptation can be reduced to a conventional online learning task, (b) we show that this reduction enables the application of classical online learning algorithms to the problem, and (c) we demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting algorithms in a variety of real world scenarios

(1) the lack of access to true test labels does not hinder the estimation of test loss, which allows the reduction of online adaptation to label shift to classical online learning; (2) we show that Follow The Leader (a classical online algorithm) is effective for adaptation under label shift, but Online Gradient Descent outperforms it in practice.

(i) we provide a theoretical analysis that shows the lack of true labels does not prevent estimation of the expected loss, and (ii) we propose and analyze two novel online algorithms for adapting to label shifts that achieve state-of-the-art performance in a variety of challenging settings.
